Design.evidence_source: In this section, we focus on results from the Self/Other condition and show they are consistent with results from Dana, Weber and Kuang (2007). We report on data from all three of our online studies. ... Across the three studies, 0.67 (Study 1), 0.72 (Study 2), and 0.65 (Study 3) of subjects in the Hidden Information condition avoid information. Across the three studies, 0.32 (Study 1), 0.33 (Study 2), and 0.33 (Study 3) of subjects choose Option A—the selfish option—in the unaligned state of the Known Information condition.

country.evidence_source: We report on data from all three of our online studies.

info_cost.evidence_source: No information about the cost of revealing information is provided in the text. Defaulting to 0.0 as per rule vu_info_cost_default.

Sample.evidence_source: The text provides proportions of choices but does not report the total number of participants (N) for any condition in any of the three studies.

N_Self_CI_Tmt.evidence_source: The text reports proportions of selfish choices in the Hidden Information condition (0.56 for Study 1, 0.59 for Study 2, 0.53 for Study 3) but does not provide the total number of participants (N) for these conditions, preventing conversion to integer counts.

N_Self_CI_Ctr.evidence_source: The text reports proportions of selfish choices in the Known Information condition (0.32 for Study 1, 0.33 for Study 2, 0.33 for Study 3) but does not provide the total number of participants (N) for these conditions, preventing conversion to integer counts.

N_Altr_CI_Ctr.evidence_source: The text does not provide the total number of participants (N_Tot_CI_Ctr) or the number of selfish choices (N_Self_CI_Ctr) as integer counts for the Known Information condition, which are necessary to derive N_Altr_CI_Ctr.

N_Tot_CI_Tmt.evidence_source: The text reports proportions of choices but does not provide the total number of participants (N) for the Hidden Information condition in any of the three studies.

N_Tot_CI_Ctr.evidence_source: The text reports proportions of choices but does not provide the total number of participants (N) for the Known Information condition in any of the three studies.
